questions.question: Which of the following pair regarding the parts of the Indian constitution is NOT correctly matched?

options.text: Services Under the Union and the States - Part XIV

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Fundamental Rights - Part III:** The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles **12 to 35**. These rights ensure the basic freedoms of citizens. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

• **Panchayats - Part IX:** Part IX of the Constitution, added by the **73rd Amendment Act of 1992**, deals with Panchayati Raj institutions (local self-governance). Articles **243 to 243-O** provide constitutional recognition to Panchayats. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

• **Elections - Part XV:** Elections in India are governed by **Part XV** of the Constitution, not Part XVII. Part XV encompasses Articles **324 to 329**, which deal with the election process and the powers of the Election Commission. **Part XVII**, on the other hand, deals with the **Official Languages**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• **Services under Union and States - Part XIV:** Part XIV of the Constitution deals with Services under the Union and the States, covering Articles **308 to 323**. It includes provisions for public services and Public Service Commissions. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Fundamental Rights:**

• Fundamental Rights are considered the cornerstone of democracy in India.

• They are enforceable by courts and include rights such as **Right to Equality**, **Right to Freedom**, **Right against Exploitation**, **Right to Freedom of Religion**, **Cultural and Educational Rights**, and **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.

• These rights are applicable to Indian citizens, and some are extended to non-citizens as well.

• **Panchayati Raj System:**

• The system of Panchayati Raj was constitutionally established to decentralize governance.

• The 73rd Amendment Act introduced a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Intermediate Panchayat, and District Panchayat.

• It empowers Panchayats to prepare plans for economic development and social justice.

• **Elections:**

• Elections in India are conducted under the supervision of the **Election Commission**, which is established by Article 324.

• India follows a **first-past-the-post system** for elections to the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.

• The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections, maintains the electoral roll, and regulates political parties.

• **Services under Union and States:**

• The Constitution provides for **All-India Services** such as the IAS, IPS, and IFS, which are common to both the Union and the States.

• State services are governed by respective state public service commissions.

• Provisions ensure impartiality, efficiency, and accountability in public administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Part XV:** This part of the Constitution is crucial for maintaining the democratic structure of the country. It includes provisions for delimitation, preparation of electoral rolls, and qualifications for membership of legislatures.

• **Part XVII:** Official Languages are covered under this part, with provisions for Hindi as the official language and safeguards for linguistic minorities.

• **Evolution of Panchayats:** The concept of Panchayati Raj dates back to the **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** (1957), which recommended a three-tier system for rural governance.

• **Judiciary and Fundamental Rights:** The judiciary acts as a guardian of Fundamental Rights, ensuring they are upheld against any violation by the state or individuals.
</ul

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'The Blue Umbrella'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Ruskin Bond** is the author of the widely acclaimed novel **'The Blue Umbrella'**. It is one of his most famous works, reflecting his signature style of storytelling with a touch of simplicity and emotional depth. 
• The novel was published in the year **1974** and is categorized as a children's book, although it appeals to readers of all ages due to its universal themes. 
• **'The Blue Umbrella'** is set in a small village in the hills of India, showcasing the rural landscape and simple village life. 
• The story revolves around a young girl named **Binya** and her fascination with a beautiful blue umbrella, which becomes the center of attention in the village. 
• The novel conveys important moral lessons such as the value of kindness, contentment, and forgiveness, which are hallmarks of **Ruskin Bond's literary works**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **About Ruskin Bond:** 
• **Ruskin Bond** is a celebrated Indian author of British descent, known for his contribution to Indian literature in English. 
• He was born on **19 May 1934**, in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, India. 
• He has written over **500 short stories, novels, and essays**, many of which are based on his experiences in the hills of India. 
• Some of his other notable works include **'Room on the Roof,' 'A Flight of Pigeons,'** and **'Rusty' series**. 
• Ruskin Bond was awarded the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1992 and the **Padma Shri** in 1999 for his contributions to literature. 
• **About 'The Blue Umbrella':** 
• The novel was adapted into a **Bollywood film** of the same name, directed by **Vishal Bhardwaj** in 2005. 
• The film won the **National Film Award for Best Children's Film** in 2007. 
• The plot highlights human emotions such as jealousy, generosity, and redemption through the journey of the protagonist, Binya, and the umbrella. 
• **Characteristics of Other Options:** 
• **Arundhati Roy:** She is the author of the Booker Prize-winning novel **'The God of Small Things'**. Her works often deal with political and social issues. 
• **R. K. Narayan:** He is best known for his **'Malgudi Days'** series and novels like **'The Guide'**. He is one of India’s most renowned authors, focusing on fictional South Indian towns. 
• **Khushwant Singh:** Known for works like **'Train to Pakistan'**, he primarily focused on historical and political themes in his writings. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Theme of 'The Blue Umbrella':** 
• The central theme of the novel is the **importance of kindness and simplicity**. It reflects the idea that material possessions are not as valuable as human relationships. 
• The story also sheds light on **human jealousy and redemption**, portraying how people can change for the better. 
• **Impact on Readers:** 
• The novel has been widely appreciated for its **engaging narrative** and **relatable characters**, making it a timeless piece of literature. 
• It continues to inspire readers across generations, especially young readers, to cultivate values of **honesty and generosity**.

questions.question: As of July 2025, Vinai Kumar Saxena is the Lieutenant Governor of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Vinai Kumar Saxena** was appointed as the **Lieutenant Governor of Delhi** on **May 23, 2022**, succeeding Anil Baijal. 
• The role of the **Lieutenant Governor (LG)** of Delhi is critical since Delhi is a **Union Territory** with a special status under Article 239AA of the **Indian Constitution**. 
• The Lieutenant Governor acts as the representative of the **President of India** in Delhi and oversees the administration of the **National Capital Territory (NCT)**. 
• **Vinai Kumar Saxena** had previously served as the **Chairman of Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** before assuming the role of LG. 
• Delhi's governance structure involves the **LG**, the Chief Minister, and the elected legislative assembly, with the LG having certain discretionary powers in administrative matters, especially relating to public order, police, and land. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **About Delhi:** 
• Delhi, officially known as the **National Capital Territory (NCT)**, is India's capital city and serves as the country's political and administrative hub. 
• It is a **Union Territory** with partial statehood, governed under Article 239AA of the Constitution. 
• Key areas such as **public order, police, and land** fall under the jurisdiction of the **Central Government** and the LG, while other matters are handled by the elected government. 
• Delhi's legislative assembly has **70 elected members**. 
• **Role and Powers of the Lieutenant Governor:** 
• The Lieutenant Governor is appointed by the **President of India** and serves as the administrative head of the Union Territory. 
• In Delhi, the LG has special powers in matters of **public order, police, and land**, which are reserved for the Central Government. 
• The LG works closely with the elected government but also has discretionary powers as granted under the Constitution. 
• **Vinai Kumar Saxena:** 
• Before being appointed as the LG of Delhi, Saxena served as the **Chairman of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)**, where he contributed significantly to promoting rural industries. 
• He has been recognized for his contributions to fostering sustainable development and rural employment in India. 
• **Governance in Other Union Territories:** 
• Unlike Delhi, most Union Territories are directly governed by the Central Government through the LG or Administrator, except for Puducherry, which also has a legislative assembly and partial statehood similar to Delhi. 
• Examples include **Ladakh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Chandigarh**, which are administered by LGs or Administrators appointed by the President. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Article 239AA:** 
• This article of the Indian Constitution provides a special status to the **National Capital Territory of Delhi**, allowing it to have a legislative assembly and council of ministers. 
• While the elected government handles most administrative matters, the LG retains authority over **public order, police, and land**. 
• **Delhi Government Structure:** 
• The Delhi government consists of the **Chief Minister**, the Council of Ministers, and the legislative assembly. 
• The LG serves as the link between the Central Government and the elected government of Delhi. 
• Disputes over jurisdiction between the LG and the Delhi government have occasionally arisen, especially in areas of administrative control. 
• **Current Developments:** 
• In recent years, the role of the LG in Delhi has been debated, leading to Supreme Court judgments clarifying the division of powers. 
• The **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Act, 2021** further defined the powers of the LG in Delhi. </ul

questions.question: Which of the following organisation/body is related to Swavalambini Programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swavalambini Programme** is an initiative aimed at promoting self-reliance and empowering individuals, especially women, by providing them with the necessary skills and resources to improve their livelihoods.
 
• **NITI Aayog**, established on **1st January 2015**, is the primary policy think tank of the Government of India and plays a significant role in designing and implementing developmental programs like Swavalambini.
 
• The Swavalambini Programme aligns with NITI Aayog's goals of fostering **sustainable development**, reducing inequalities, and enhancing socio-economic growth through skill development and entrepreneurship promotion.
 
• Under this program, NITI Aayog collaborates with state governments, private organizations, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to implement and monitor its initiatives effectively.
 
• By focusing on capacity building and entrepreneurship, Swavalambini helps individuals become financially independent and contributes to the larger goal of **India's economic development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog:**

 
 
• NITI Aayog stands for **National Institution for Transforming India**. It replaced the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The primary aim is to act as a **think tank** and policy advisor to the Central and State governments, focusing on fostering cooperative federalism.
 
• It emphasizes **bottom-up planning** rather than the traditional top-down approach.
 
• Key initiatives by NITI Aayog include **Aspirational Districts Programme**, **Atal Innovation Mission**, and **Digital India initiatives**.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Bodies in the Options:**
 
 
• **NHRC (National Human Rights Commission):** Established in **1993**, NHRC focuses on the protection and promotion of **human rights** in India. It does not deal with self-reliance programs like Swavalambini.
 
• **CIC (Central Information Commission):** The CIC was constituted under the **Right to Information Act, 2005** to ensure transparency and accountability in governance. It is unrelated to the Swavalambini Programme.
 
• **NDMA (National Disaster Management Authority):** NDMA is responsible for disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response. It does not directly deal with skill development or livelihood programs.
 
 
 
• **Focus of Swavalambini Programme:**
 
 
• The program is aimed at **empowering marginalized sections** of society, particularly women and youth, through skill development and entrepreneurship training.
 
• It seeks to create an enabling environment for individuals to achieve **economic independence** and self-reliance.
 
• Such programs are often implemented in partnership with **state governments**, NGOs, and private sector entities.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples:**
 
 
• Similar self-reliance initiatives include **Skill India Mission**, **Start-Up India**, and **Stand-Up India** programs, which aim to enhance employability and entrepreneurship among youth.
 
• These programs align with India’s **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 8, which focuses on decent work and economic growth.

questions.question: Who won the first season of Ranji trophy in 1934-35?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Ranji Trophy** is a domestic first-class cricket championship played in India, named after the famous Indian cricketer **Kumar Shri Ranjitsinhji**.

• The inaugural season of the Ranji Trophy was held in the year **1934-35**, and the final match took place between **Bombay** and **Northern India**.

• **Bombay** won the first-ever Ranji Trophy championship by defeating Northern India in the final. The final was played at the **Bombay Gymkhana Ground**.

• Bombay (now Mumbai) is historically one of the strongest teams in Indian domestic cricket, having won the **Ranji Trophy a record number of times**.

• The championship is played in a **knockout format**, and later evolved to include a league stage to identify the top teams for the finals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Ranji Trophy Format:** 

• The competition initially followed a knockout format but later adopted a combination of league and knockout stages to ensure fair play and enhance competitiveness.

• Teams represent different states, regions, and cricket associations in India.

• The tournament is governed by the **Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)**.

• **Significance of Bombay's Victory:** 

• Bombay's victory in the inaugural season marked the beginning of its dominance in Indian domestic cricket.

• Bombay went on to become one of the most successful teams in the history of the Ranji Trophy, with over **40 titles** to its name.

• **Notable Players:** 

• Several legendary cricketers have represented Bombay in the Ranji Trophy, including **Sunil Gavaskar**, **Dilip Vengsarkar**, **Sachin Tendulkar**, and **Ajinkya Rahane**.

• The Ranji Trophy has been a platform for nurturing young talent and preparing players for international cricket.

• **Historical Context:** 

• The Ranji Trophy was introduced to promote cricket in India and provide domestic players with competitive match experience.

• The tournament has contributed significantly to the development of Indian cricket and the identification of future stars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Notable Teams:** 

• **Madras** (now Tamil Nadu), **Holkar**, and **Delhi** have also been prominent teams in the history of the Ranji Trophy.

• Holkar, a dominant team in the early years, produced cricket legends like **C.K. Nayudu**.

• **Modern Era of Ranji Trophy:** 

• Over time, the format has evolved to include a group stage followed by knockouts, allowing more teams to participate.

• The Ranji Trophy continues to be a critical tournament for Indian cricket, serving as a stepping stone for players aspiring to represent the national team.

• **Records and Achievements:** 

• Bombay holds the record for the most consecutive Ranji Trophy titles, winning **15 straight championships** from 1958-59 to 1972-73.

• Players like **Wasim Jaffer** and **Amol Muzumdar** hold individual records for runs and centuries in the tournament.

</ul

questions.question: The "Mission Amrit Sarovar" initiative is anchored by the ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **"Mission Amrit Sarovar"** initiative was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** to address the issue of water conservation and rejuvenation of water bodies across India. 
• This mission is aimed at creating and restoring at least **75 water bodies in each district** of the country as part of the celebration of **Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav**. 
• The initiative focuses on promoting **community participation** and involvement of local stakeholders, including **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, to ensure the sustainability of water bodies. 
• The mission is aligned with the broader goals of achieving water security and promoting sustainable development by addressing **water scarcity** and improving irrigation facilities. 
• The Ministry of Rural Development plays a pivotal role in the implementation of this initiative by coordinating with various state governments and leveraging **existing schemes like MGNREGS (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme)** for funding and manpower. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Key Objectives of Mission Amrit Sarovar:** 
• To conserve water by creating and rejuvenating **75 water bodies per district** as a tribute to India's 75 years of independence. 
• To enhance the availability of water for **agricultural, domestic, and ecological purposes**, thereby contributing to water security. 
• To involve local communities in water conservation efforts, ensuring the **sustainability and upkeep** of water bodies. 
• **Role of the Ministry of Rural Development:** 
• Acts as the nodal agency for the mission and provides guidance and support to state governments and local bodies. 
• Utilizes existing **development schemes**, such as MGNREGS, for funding the construction and restoration of water bodies. 
• Collaborates with other ministries, such as the Ministry of Jal Shakti and Ministry of Environment, for technical expertise and integrated efforts. 
• **Other Related Initiatives:** 
• **Atal Bhujal Yojana:** A scheme aimed at improving groundwater management in critical areas of India through community participation. 
• **Jal Shakti Abhiyan:** A campaign to promote water conservation and rainwater harvesting through a **time-bound, mission-mode approach**. 
• **Catch the Rain Campaign:** An initiative to improve water harvesting structures during the pre-monsoon and monsoon periods. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Key Features of Mission Amrit Sarovar:** 
• Focuses on **water conservation** through the construction and restoration of water bodies. 
• Emphasizes **community participation** to ensure long-term sustainability. 
• Promotes the use of technology, including **GIS mapping** and **remote sensing**, for identifying and monitoring water bodies. 
• Aims to improve **livelihood opportunities** in rural areas by integrating with schemes like MGNREGS. 
• **Significance of Water Conservation:** 
• Addresses the issue of **water scarcity**, which affects agriculture, drinking water supply, and ecological balance. 
• Ensures the availability of water resources for **future generations**. 
• Improves **agricultural productivity** by providing reliable water sources for irrigation. </ul

questions.question: The International Hockey Federation, was founded in Paris in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1924**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** was founded in **1924** in **Paris, France**. This was a pivotal step in organizing field hockey on a global scale. 
• The establishment of the FIH was driven by the need for a governing body to oversee the rules and regulations of field hockey and promote the sport internationally. 
• Field hockey was already popular in several countries, but the **creation of FIH** provided a standardized structure for international competitions. 
• The founding members of the FIH included nations such as **Austria, Belgium, Czechoslovakia, France, Hungary, Spain, and Switzerland**. These countries contributed to the development of the sport globally. 
• Since its inception, the FIH has played a significant role in organizing major hockey tournaments, including the **Hockey World Cup** and the **Olympic Games hockey competitions**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Field Hockey History:** 
• Field hockey traces its origins back to ancient civilizations, including **Egypt**, **Greece**, and **Persia**. The modern form of the game emerged in the late 19th century in **England**. 
• The first field hockey club, **Blackheath Hockey Club**, was established in London in **1861**. 
• Field hockey gained prominence as a competitive sport, leading to its inclusion in the **1908 Summer Olympics**. 
• **FIH's Role:** 
• The FIH governs the rules of field hockey globally and ensures fair play and uniform standards during international tournaments. 
• It is responsible for organizing events such as the **Hockey World Cup**, **Champions Trophy**, and **Pro League**, which showcase the best teams from across the world. 
• The FIH also promotes field hockey through development programs, increasing participation in countries where hockey is less established. 
• **FIH Headquarters:** 
• The headquarters of the FIH is located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, a hub for international sports organizations. 
• The FIH moved its headquarters from Brussels, Belgium, to Lausanne in **2005** to align with other sports federations. 
• **Major Milestones in Field Hockey:** 
• Field hockey was first included in the **Olympic Games** in **1908**, with men's teams competing. 
• Women's hockey made its Olympic debut in **1980** during the Moscow Games. 
• The **Hockey World Cup**, introduced in **1971**, is one of the most prestigious tournaments organized by the FIH. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The FIH was established to provide a structured organization for field hockey, which was growing rapidly in popularity. 
• The founding year, **1924**, marked the formalization of the sport's governance on a global level. 
• Since its creation, the FIH has expanded to include more than **130 member nations**, showcasing the global appeal of field hockey. 
• The FIH continues to play a critical role in promoting field hockey and organizing international competitions that bring together players and fans worldwide. </ul

questions.question: Narayanrao Rajhauns, also known as Bal Gandharava, was a celebrated exponent of which state's musical tradition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Narayanrao Rajhauns**, popularly known as **Bal Gandharva**, was a celebrated figure in the musical and theatrical traditions of **Maharashtra**.

• He was a prominent exponent of **Natya Sangeet**, a unique genre of musical theatre that originated in Maharashtra and combines classical music with theatrical performances.

• Bal Gandharva gained immense popularity for his portrayal of female roles in Marathi theatre during the early 20th century, a time when women were not allowed to act on stage.

• The name **“Gandharva”** (meaning celestial musician) was given to him by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, reflecting his divine singing talent and contribution to music.

• His contributions to Maharashtra’s cultural heritage were immense, and he remains a revered figure in the state’s artistic history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Natya Sangeet:**

• It is a form of **musical theatre** that blends classical Indian music with dramatic storytelling.

• Natya Sangeet evolved in Maharashtra during the late 19th and early 20th centuries and remains an integral part of Marathi culture.

• Bal Gandharva played a crucial role in popularizing Natya Sangeet by performing in numerous Marathi plays, such as *Sangeet Saubhadra* and *Sangeet Manapman*.

• **Bal Gandharva’s Legacy:**

• He is remembered not only for his singing but also for his dedication to the arts, often financing plays and productions at great personal expense.

• His life and contributions have been commemorated in various ways, including the **Bal Gandharva Rang Mandir**, a theatre in Pune named in his honor.

• **Maharashtra’s Musical Tradition:**

• Maharashtra has a rich cultural heritage, with contributions to Indian classical music, folk music, and theatrical traditions.

• The fort is known for its unique architecture, including a prominent **Ashokan Pillar** brought from Ambala and placed on top of the fort.

• He shifted the capital from Tughlaqabad to **Firozabad**. 
• **Ashokan Pillar:**

• It played a crucial role in the administration and defense of the empire during the 14th century. 
• **Local Beliefs:** 
• The fort is associated with **supernatural folklore**, where locals believe that djinns inhabit its ruins. 
• Even today, people visit the fort to offer letters and prayers to the djinns, seeking blessings and solutions to their problems. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Tughlaq Dynasty:** The Tughlaq dynasty was a prominent ruling dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, known for its administrative reforms and architectural achievements. 
• **Firozabad:** The city of Firozabad, established by Feroz Shah Tughlaq, was one of the seven historic cities of Delhi. 
• **Preservation:** Although in ruins today, the Feroz Shah Kotla Fort is maintained by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, highlighting its cultural and historical importance. 
• **Tourism:** The fort is a popular tourist attraction, offering insights into the Tughlaq era's history and architecture. </ul

questions.question: A communication satellite acts like a television tower placed at a height of __________ km.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**36000 km**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• A **communication satellite** acts like a television tower placed at a significant altitude to facilitate communication over a wide area. 
• The altitude of a communication satellite is generally at **36,000 km above the Earth’s surface**, which is known as a **geostationary orbit**. 
• A satellite in a geostationary orbit appears stationary relative to the Earth’s rotation, ensuring **continuous coverage** of a specific area on the Earth. 
• This orbit is ideal for communication purposes as it allows satellites to cover a large area and provide services like television broadcasting, telecommunication, and internet access. 
• The specific altitude of 36,000 km ensures that the satellite’s orbital period matches the rotation period of the Earth, i.e., 24 hours. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Geostationary Orbit:** 
• Geostationary orbit is located at an altitude of **approximately 35,786 km** above the equator. 
• Satellites in this orbit revolve around the Earth at the same speed as the Earth rotates, making them appear stationary from the ground. 
• This orbit is extensively used for **communication satellites** like television, telecommunication, weather monitoring, and GPS services. 
• **Types of Satellite Orbits:** 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Located at altitudes between **160 km to 2,000 km**, used for Earth observation and telecommunication. 
• **Medium Earth Orbit (MEO):** Located at altitudes between **2,000 km to 35,786 km**, often used for navigation satellites. 
• **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Located at around **36,000 km**, ideal for communication satellites. 
• **Functions of Communication Satellites:** 
• Provide **television broadcasting**, satellite radio, and internet access. 
• Facilitate long-distance **telecommunication** and mobile services. 
• Enable global coverage for **weather forecasting**, disaster management, and GPS navigation systems. 
• **Examples of Communication Satellites:** 
• **INSAT series:** India’s communication satellites used for television broadcasting and meteorological purposes. 
• **GSAT series:** Another set of Indian communication satellites providing telecommunication services. 
• **Intelsat:** International satellites used for global communication services. 
• **Important Facts:** 
• The concept of geostationary satellites was first proposed by scientist **Arthur C. Clarke** in **1945**. 
• The first geostationary communication satellite was **SYNCOM 3**, launched by the USA in **1964**. 
• India’s first communication satellite was **INSAT-1A**, launched in **1982**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Why 36,000 km is chosen:** 
• The altitude ensures the satellite’s orbital period matches Earth’s rotational period (**24 hours**). 
• This allows for **stable communication** without the need for constant tracking. 
• **Applications:** 
• Used for **live television broadcasts**, including sports events and news. 
• Critical for **disaster management** and emergency communication. 
• Vital for modern navigation systems and **global internet connectivity**. 
• **Challenges:** 
• High cost of satellite launches and maintenance. 
• Risk of **space debris** affecting operational satellites. 
• Signal latency due to the large distance from Earth.

questions.question: The Aditya L-1 mission of ISRO was launched in which of the following year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **Aditya L-1 mission** was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** in the year **2023**. 
• The mission is India's first dedicated solar observation mission, aimed at studying the **Sun's corona, chromosphere, and solar winds**. 
• Aditya L-1 was launched on **September 2, 2023**, using the **PSLV-C57** rocket from the **Sriharikota spaceport**. 
• The spacecraft is designed to be placed in a **halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1)** of the Sun-Earth system, approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth. 
• The mission aims to provide crucial information about **solar activities** and their impact on Earth's **space weather** systems. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Aditya L-1 Mission Objectives:** 
• To study the dynamics of the **solar corona**, which is the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere. 
• To understand the processes behind the **solar wind** and its interaction with the Earth's magnetosphere. 
• To observe the **photosphere and chromosphere** of the Sun and analyze their behavior. 
• To monitor **solar flares** and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) that influence space weather. 
• To investigate particle behavior in the Earth's vicinity caused by solar activities. 
• **Lagrange Point 1 (L1):** 
• Lagrange Point 1 (L1) is a stable location in space where the gravitational forces of the Sun and Earth balance the orbital motion of a satellite. 
• It allows continuous observation of the Sun without interruptions caused by Earth's rotation or other celestial movements. 
• The L1 point is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth in the direction of the Sun. 
• **Scientific Instruments on Aditya L-1:** 
• **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC):** Designed to study the solar corona and measure its magnetic field. 
• **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT):** Observes the photosphere and chromosphere in ultraviolet wavelengths. 
• **Aditya Solar Wind Particle Experiment (ASPEX):** Studies solar wind particles and their properties. 
• **Plasma Analyser Package for Aditya (PAPA):** Analyzes plasma in the solar wind. 
• **Significance of Aditya L-1:** 
• It is India's first solar observation mission, marking a major milestone in space research. 
• The data collected will help scientists better understand **space weather phenomena**, which can impact satellite operations and communication systems. 
• It contributes to global efforts in studying the Sun, alongside missions like NASA's **Parker Solar Probe** and ESA's **Solar Orbiter**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **PSLV-C57 Rocket:** 
• The Aditya L-1 mission was launched using the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)**, a trusted workhorse of ISRO. 
• PSLV-C57 ensured precise placement of the spacecraft in its intended trajectory toward the L1 point. 
• **Space Weather Impact:** 
• Space weather events, such as solar storms, can disrupt **satellite communication, navigation systems, and power grids**. 
• Understanding these phenomena is crucial for mitigating their effects on technological systems. 
• **Global Collaborations:** 
• Aditya L-1 complements international missions like NASA's **Parker Solar Probe**, which studies the Sun's atmosphere and solar wind. 
• Such missions contribute to a collective understanding of the Sun and its influence on the solar system. </ul

__

• **Chandrayaan-2** was India's second lunar exploration mission developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.

• The mission consisted of three components: an **Orbiter**, a **Lander** named **Vikram**, and a **Rover** named **Pragyan**.

• The **Lander Vikram** was named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space program.

• The **Rover Pragyan** (meaning 'wisdom' in Sanskrit) was designed to analyze the lunar surface and send data back to Earth.

• The mission aimed to explore the **South Polar Region of the Moon**, which had not been extensively studied by previous missions.

• **ISRO launched Chandrayaan-2** on **22 July 2019** from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota using the GSLV Mk III rocket.

• The **Orbiter** was equipped with eight scientific instruments to study the Moon from its orbit.

• The **Lander Vikram** was designed to perform a soft landing on the Moon's surface.

• Unfortunately, the lander lost communication with ISRO during its final descent, around 2.1 kilometers above the lunar surface.

• Despite this setback, the mission was considered a significant achievement for India's space exploration efforts.

• **Rover Pragyan:**

• The **Rover Pragyan** had a mission life of 14 Earth days and was equipped with two instruments to study the lunar soil and terrain.

• Its goal was to analyze the chemical composition of the Moon's surface and detect elements such as magnesium, aluminum, and silicon.

• However, it could not perform its tasks as the lander did not successfully deploy it on the lunar surface.

• **Significance of Chandrayaan-2:**

• The data from the Orbiter continues to be used for scientific research and analysis.

• India's first lunar mission, Chandrayaan-1, was launched on **22 October 2008**.

• It discovered water molecules on the Moon, a groundbreaking finding in lunar science.

questions.question: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority was established in India in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** was established by the Government of India in the year **2003**.
 
• The PFRDA was initially set up as an interim regulator for the **National Pension System (NPS)**, which was introduced for government employees except for the armed forces.
 
• Its primary role is to **regulate and develop the pension sector** in India to promote old-age income security.
 
• In **2013**, the PFRDA Act was passed by Parliament, giving statutory status to the authority. This provided a legal framework for the regulation of the NPS and other pension schemes.
 
• The PFRDA is responsible for overseeing the operations of pension fund managers, ensuring the protection of subscribers' interests, and promoting transparency in the pension sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Pension System (NPS):**

 
 
• The **NPS** was launched on **1 January 2004** for government employees and later extended to all citizens in **2009**.
 
• It is a voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme designed to enable subscribers to make systematic savings during their working life.
 
• The NPS offers two types of accounts: **Tier I** (mandatory retirement account) and **Tier II** (voluntary savings account).
 
• Subscribers can choose from various pension fund managers and investment options as per their risk appetite.
 
 
 
• **PFRDA Act, 2013:**
 
 
• The **PFRDA Act, 2013** provides a statutory framework for the functioning of the PFRDA and the regulation of the pension sector in India.
 
• It allows the PFRDA to regulate all pension schemes except those under the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) and other social security schemes under the government.
 
• The Act also ensures the protection of subscribers' interests by mandating transparency and fair practices in the pension sector.
 
 
 
• **Functions of PFRDA:**
 
 
• Regulating and promoting the **National Pension System (NPS)**.
 
• Ensuring the safety and growth of pension funds through stringent regulations.
 
• Approving and monitoring **Pension Fund Managers (PFMs)** and other intermediaries.
 
• Encouraging financial literacy about retirement planning and pensions.
 
 
 
• **Other Pension Schemes Managed by PFRDA:**
 
 
• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY):** A government-backed pension scheme for the unorganized sector launched in **2015**.
 
• **Corporate NPS:** A variant of the NPS designed for employees of corporate entities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **PFRDA** plays a crucial role in ensuring **retirement income security** for Indian citizens by promoting and regulating a sustainable and transparent pension market.
 
• The **NPS Trust**, under the PFRDA, manages the funds contributed by subscribers and ensures they are invested appropriately.
 
• The PFRDA is headquartered in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• The **Swavalamban Scheme**, which aimed to provide a pension scheme for workers in the unorganized sector, was later merged with the **Atal Pension Yojana**.

questions.question: Which of the following is referred as Public sector unit (PSU) disinvestment?

options.text: Allowing direct foreign direct investment in PSU
Allowing indirect foreign direct investment in PSU

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sale of shares in PSU**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Public Sector Unit (PSU) disinvestment** refers to the process of the **government selling its equity stake** in Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to private entities, institutional investors, or the general public.

• The primary objective of disinvestment is to **reduce the fiscal burden** on the government, improve the efficiency and competitiveness of PSUs, and to mobilize funds for other developmental projects.

• This process is often carried out by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (**DIPAM**) under the Ministry of Finance in India.

• PSU disinvestment is categorized based on the percentage of shares sold: **minority disinvestment** (government retains majority control), **majority disinvestment** (government loses majority control), and **complete privatization** (government exits ownership entirely).

• The sale of shares can take place via **Initial Public Offerings (IPO)**, **Follow-on Public Offerings (FPO)**, **strategic sale**, or **offer for sale (OFS)** mechanisms. *Hence, the correct answer is Sale of shares in PSU__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__

• **Objective of Disinvestment:**

• To improve **financial health** by reducing fiscal deficits and generating non-tax revenue for the government.

• To enhance the **efficiency and professionalism** of PSUs by involving private management and reducing bureaucratic control.

• To meet international obligations such as **World Trade Organization (WTO)** commitments by reducing state interference in industries.

• **Methods of Disinvestment:**

• **IPO:** Offering shares of a PSU to the public for the first time.

• **OFS:** Selling shares on the stock exchange platform to institutional and retail investors.

• **Strategic Sale:** Selling a substantial portion of government shares along with management control to a private entity.

• **ETFs:** Creating Exchange Traded Funds to pool PSU shares and offer them to investors.

• **Examples of PSU Disinvestment in India:**

• In 2021, the government disinvested its stake in **Air India**, transferring ownership to the Tata Group.

• The **LIC IPO** in 2022 marked one of the largest disinvestments in India, raising significant funds.

• Other notable examples include the disinvestment of PSUs like **Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL)** and **Container Corporation of India (CONCOR)**.

• **Challenges in Disinvestment:**

• Resistance from employees and trade unions fearing **job losses** and changes in work culture.

• Unfavorable market conditions may lead to **lower valuations** of PSUs.

• Concerns over **monopoly creation** if strategic sales lead to market concentration.

• Political opposition to privatization as it may be perceived as selling national assets to private entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM):**

• Established to manage the **disinvestment process** in India and oversee the sale of equity in PSUs.

• Responsible for formulating policies and guidelines for disinvestment.

• **National Investment Fund (NIF):**

• Created in 2005 to channelize disinvestment proceeds for **social welfare projects** and capital investment in PSUs.

• The fund is managed by professional asset managers to ensure efficient utilization.

• **Fiscal Targets:**

• The government sets annual disinvestment targets in the **Union Budget** to raise funds for fiscal management.

• For example, in FY 2021-22, the disinvestment target was set at **INR 1.75 lakh crore**.

``

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15% of the total strength of the House of the People**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** introduced a cap on the size of the Council of Ministers in India.

• As per the amendment, the total number of ministers, including the **Prime Minister**, in the **Council of Ministers** cannot exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.

• This limit applies to both the Union and State governments, ensuring that the size of the executive remains proportionate to the legislature.

• The amendment was introduced to curb the practice of unnecessarily expanding the Council of Ministers, which could lead to inefficiency and misuse of public resources.

• This provision is now enshrined under **Article 75(1A)** of the Constitution of India for the Union government and **Article 164(1A)** for State governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:**

• This amendment was enacted to bring about political stability and prevent defections and arbitrary expansion of the Council of Ministers.

• It also added provisions to strengthen the **anti-defection law** by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial positions or other remunerative posts.

• The amendment mandates that the total number of ministers in a state, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed **15%** of the total members of the Legislative Assembly.

• **Article 75(1A):**

• This article specifies the limit on the size of the Council of Ministers at the Union level.

• It ensures that the executive branch operates within a defined framework to avoid inefficiency.

• **Article 164(1A):**

• This article applies the same 15% rule to the Council of Ministers at the state level, including the Chief Minister.

• This ensures uniformity in governance practices across the Union and the States.

• **Reasons for the 91st Amendment:**

• The amendment was introduced to address issues related to political instability caused by frequent defections and coalition pressures.

• It aimed to prevent the misuse of ministerial appointments as a tool to gain political support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Anti-Defection Law:**

• The 91st Amendment strengthened the **anti-defection provisions** outlined in the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.

• It barred defectors from holding ministerial or remunerative positions for the remainder of the legislative term.

• **Impact of the 91st Amendment:**

• It reduced the size of bloated Cabinets, improving efficiency and reducing the financial burden on the exchequer.

• It promoted political discipline and curbed opportunistic defections.

• **Exceptions:**

• In cases where the total strength of the legislature is very small, states may have a minimum of 12 ministers, regardless of the 15% cap.

questions.question: Which type of reactions are driven by the energy provided by ATP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endothermic reactions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** is the primary energy currency of the cell. It provides the necessary energy to drive many biochemical reactions, especially those that are **endothermic (energy-absorbing)**.

• **Endothermic reactions** are chemical reactions that require an input of energy to proceed. In biological systems, this energy is often supplied by the hydrolysis of ATP.

• During ATP hydrolysis, the bond between the terminal phosphate group is broken, releasing approximately **30.5 kJ/mol of energy**. This energy is utilized to fuel reactions that would not occur spontaneously.

• Examples of processes driven by ATP in endothermic reactions include **protein synthesis, active transport of molecules across membranes, and muscle contraction**.

questions.question: Some of the earliest works in Tamil, known as Sangam literature, were composed around _________ years ago.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2300 years ago**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sangam literature** refers to the earliest known Tamil texts, which are considered the foundation of Tamil culture and heritage. These works date back approximately **2300 years**.
 
• The Sangam era is believed to have existed between the **3rd century BCE to the 3rd century CE**. The term "Sangam" refers to academies or assemblies of Tamil poets and scholars during this period.
 
• Sangam literature consists of **poems and prose** that focus on themes like **love, war, governance, and ethics**. These texts are divided into three categories: **Aham (love and emotion), Puram (war, heroism, and external events), and narrative epics**.
 
• Key works of Sangam literature include **Tolkappiyam** (an ancient Tamil grammar text), **Kuruntokai**, **Akananuru**, **Purananuru**, and **Pattuppāṭṭu**.
 
• The Sangam period is considered a golden age in Tamil history, marking advancements in **literature, trade, governance, and culture**. It is also a testament to the rich linguistic and philosophical traditions of ancient Tamil society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sangam Period Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Sangam period corresponds to the **Iron Age** in South India, during which Tamil civilization flourished.
 
• It was marked by organized kingdoms such as the **Chera, Chola, and Pandya dynasties**, which contributed significantly to Tamil art, literature, and trade.
 
• Trade routes during the Sangam era connected Tamil regions to **Rome, Egypt, and Southeast Asia**, fostering cultural and economic exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Sangam Literature:**
 
 
• Sangam literature offers insights into the **social structure, economy, and religious practices** of ancient Tamil society.
 
• These texts preserve ancient Tamil grammar, vocabulary, and poetic traditions, serving as a linguistic treasure for modern scholars.
 
• Sangam works also highlight the importance of **nature and human emotions**, reflecting the deep connection between people and their environment.
 
 
 
• **Key Characteristics of Sangam Literature:**
 
 
• Sangam texts are known for their **brevity, imagery, and lyrical beauty**. They often employ metaphors and similes to convey complex emotions.
 
• The literature is divided into **Akam (inner) and Puram (outer) themes**, representing private and public aspects of life.
 
• These works also emphasize ethical values, such as **honesty, bravery, and compassion**, which were revered in Tamil society.
 
 
 
• **Preservation and Study:**
 
 
• Sangam literature has been preserved through palm-leaf manuscripts and oral traditions. Modern scholars have studied these texts to reconstruct ancient Tamil history.
 
• The Tamil Nadu government and academic institutions have undertaken efforts to **digitize and translate Sangam texts** for global accessibility.
 
• These texts are celebrated annually during **Tamil Literature Day**, promoting awareness of Tamil heritage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **2300 years ago** is a widely accepted timeline for the Sangam period based on archaeological evidence and cross-references from ancient texts like **Ashokan inscriptions**.
 
• The Sangam period is distinct from later Tamil literature, such as the **Bhakti movement** poetry and epics like **Kamba Ramayanam**.
 
• Sangam works have influenced classical Tamil art forms like **Bharatanatyam**, folk music, and temple architecture.
 
• UNESCO has recognized Tamil as one of the **oldest surviving classical languages**, with Sangam literature as its primary evidence.
